name: Gabbro-Vigil
description: Gabbro-Vigil is a moon-sized shard of dark stone adrift in the cold outer system, its face so densely cratered that the horizon looks like frozen surf. Four billion years of impacts have ground its surface into fine gray regolith that clings to everything and lets go of nothing, and beneath it lies bedrock veined with titanium. The sun appears here as little more than the brightest star, casting long, colorless shadows across wastes that have never known weather.

Silence on Gabbro-Vigil is total, the kind that presses against the ears until visitors invent sounds to fill it. Footprints last forever, each bootfall a small permanent event, and the slow rotation means dawn takes hours to crawl across the crater rims. At night the temperature plunges until the regolith itself crackles, a faint ticking heard through suit contact like the world counting to itself.

Surveyors named it for the vigil they imagined it keeping over the system's edge, but the name took on weight when an automated navigation beacon was found standing in the shadow of its largest crater, transmitting on frequencies no registry claims. Its casing is pitted with micrometeorite scars centuries deep, yet it has never once missed a scheduled pulse. Who placed it, and for whom, remains unanswered.

For tramp freighters running dark routes through the outer system, the beacon makes Gabbro-Vigil the only reliable waypoint for a thousand light-hours, and its shallow gravity well makes it a perfect place to hide. Smugglers cache fuel in lava tubes along the terminator; patrol cutters check those tubes anyway. All parties agree on one thing: whatever the beacon is guiding toward, no one has followed the bearing past the system's edge and come back to say.
